title: Principality of Minsk
capsule: The Principality of Minsk emerged around 1101 when Vseslav of Polotsk died and his lands were divided among his sons, with Gleb Vseslavich receiving the Minsk region. Centered on the Svislach and Drut river basins and including towns such as Barysaw and Orsha, the principality carved out a precarious existence between Kievan suzerainty and expanding Lithuanian power, frequently raiding neighbors as Gleb did against his own brothers before his capture by Vladimir Monomakh (d. 1119). By the 13th century Lithuanian expansion reduced the Minsk princes to vassalage; a 1326 treaty with Novgorod was signed on behalf of Gediminas of Lithuania by the Minsk ruler, confirming effective Lithuanian absorption. The principality ceased as a distinct entity with the Union of Horodło in 1413.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The extent of the Principality of Minsk is poorly attested; its borders shifted continuously and no administrative documents survive, leaving modern reconstructions reliant on chronicle references to individual towns and battles.
